summary: Mamata Dash is an Indologist who studied at Ravenshaw Girls' High School and Utkal University.

Mamoru Tonami (1937–2024) was a scholar of sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Ichisada Miyazaki, earning a doctorate in 1987, and later held professorships at Kyoto University and Otani University.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society and as Co-ordinator for DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University.

Mandan Mishra (1929–2001) worked in Indology and philosophy. He held positions at the University of Rajasthan, served as Principal at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University (~1967–1989), and was Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1996–1999).

Manfred B. Steger is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi and Rutgers University, and held professorial posts at RMIT University (2005–2011) and the University of Hawaiʻi (2011–2016).

Manfred Mayrhofer (1926–2011) was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein, later holding full professorships at Saarland University and the University of Vienna.

Manfred Taube (1928–2021) specialized in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller, where he later became Professor of Tibetan and Mongolian Philology in 1991.

Mangal Deva Shastri (1890–1976) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his D.Phil. from the University of Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and served as Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from around 1931 to 1946.

Manik Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He has been affiliated with the Lotus Research Centre, the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Heidelberg.
Manlio Iofrida is a philosopher who studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore from ~1970 to 1974. He held academic posts at the University of Pisa and the University of Bologna.

Manshi Kiyozawa (1863–1903) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo under Ernest Francisco Fenollosa. He served as the first dean and founding president of Otani University from ~1901 to 1902.
Manu Leumann (1889–1977) was a linguist and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Munich from ~1922 to 1927 and at the University of Zurich from ~1927 to 1959.
Manudeva was an Indologist and linguist who studied under the traditional teacher Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa (Bālaśarman Pāyaguṇḍe).

Marc Aurel Stein (1862–1943) was a scholar of archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He completed a PhD at Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and held posts at the University of the Punjab and the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Lausanne in 2016 under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies under Matthew T. Kapstein and was also taught by scholars including Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Cohen (1884–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1911–1954) and the University of Paris (~1919–1954).

Marcel Granet (1884–1940) was a sinologist and scholar of religious studies who studied under Émile Durkheim and Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises.
Marcel Hofinger was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the Catholic University of Louvain under Étienne Lamotte.

Marcel Mauss (1872–1950) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under Émile Durkheim and Sylvain Lévi. He served as Directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and held the Chair of Sociology at the Collège de France.
